html:
The Pakajaqi, or Pacajes, were an Aymara-speaking people and lordship on the high plain south of Lake Titicaca, in today's La Paz department of Bolivia, near the ruins of Tiwanaku. Their main town was Caquiaviri.

They were one of the Aymara kingdoms that rose after Tiwanaku fell. They herded llamas and alpacas and grew potatoes and quinoa. The Inca brought them under their rule in the 1400s, and later the Spanish made Pacajes a province whose men were drafted for the mines of Potosí. Their neighbours to the north were the Qolla and the Lupaqa. The map shows the same people in later years as Pacaxes.
